label: When axes are tilted
subgoals: A rotated conic contains an xy term.
The shape is the same as an unrotated conic.
The coordinate axes no longer line up with the conic axes.

visual.title: The xy term tilts the axes
visual.caption: An xy term rotates the principal axes without changing the conic type. For x² + xy + y² = 1 the discriminant is −3, so the curve is still an ellipse. Its principal axes lie at 45° to the coordinate axes.

predict.question: What does the xy term do to x² + xy + y² = 1?
options: It changes the ellipse into a hyperbola
It rotates the principal axes by 45°
It moves the centre away from the origin
predict.explain: The discriminant is 1 − 4 = −3, so the curve is still an ellipse. The xy term rotates its principal axes to 45° and −45°. It does not change the centre, which remains the origin.

label: The discriminant
subgoals: For Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0 compute B^2 - 4AC.
A negative value means an ellipse or a point.
Zero can mean a parabola or parallel lines, and a positive value can mean a hyperbola or intersecting lines.

label: Finding the angle
subgoals: The rotation angle satisfies tan(2 theta) = B / (A - C).
Rotating by that angle removes the xy term.
After rotation the conic can be read in standard form.
